deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the draft of the thermodynamic preliminary to Riemann's 1860 paper 'Ueber die Fortpflanzung ebener Luftwellen von endlicher Schwingungsweite'. The previous page argues that heat exchange in sound or air waves is negligible, so the pressure-density relation must be the adiabatic one, not Boyle-Mariotte. This page derives that adiabatic law.

(1) Ideal-gas law (Mariotte/Boyle plus Gay-Lussac). Let v be the specific volume (volume per unit weight), p the pressure and T the absolute temperature (counted from -273 C). Then p v = R T, i.e. log p + log v = log T + const.

(2) Treat T = T(p,v). Let c be the specific heat at constant pressure and c' the specific heat at constant volume. Note that Riemann's c is c_p and his c' is c_v.
- Changing v by dv at constant p changes T by (dT/dv)_p dv and costs heat c (dT/dv)_p dv.
- Changing p by dp at constant v costs heat c' (dT/dp)_v dp.
- Total heat absorbed: dQ = c (dT/dv) dv + c' (dT/dp) dp.

(3) From (1), dlogT/dlogv = dlogT/dlogp = 1, so dT/dv = T/v and dT/dp = T/p. Hence dQ = T (c dlog v + c' dlog p).

(4) Adiabatic condition dQ = 0 gives dlog p = -(c/c') dlog v.

(5) Following Poisson, assume k = c/c' is independent of temperature and pressure. Integrating gives log p = -k log v + const, i.e. p v^k = const (Poisson's adiabatic law).

(6) The page breaks off at the start of a sentence citing the recent experiments of Regnault, Joule and W. Thomson, which presumably confirm this assumption.

Purpose: this supplies the pressure-density law p proportional to rho^k used in the 1860 shock-wave/characteristics paper.
errors: No mathematical errors. Each step follows from p v proportional to T, and the heat expression is the standard caloric-theory form dQ = c_p (dT/dv)_p dv + c_v (dT/dp)_v dp.
Notational point only: c denotes c_p and c' denotes c_v, the reverse of a common modern convention. With this convention k = c/c' = gamma > 1, consistent with the formulas.

results.what: Ideal gas law in logarithmic form: log p + log v = log T + const
Heat absorbed dQ = T (c_p dlog v + c_v dlog p); adiabatic condition gives dlog p = -gamma dlog v, hence p v^gamma = const
results.usually_credited_to: Laplace (1816) and Poisson (1823); Riemann himself cites Poisson

deep.surprise_reason: Routine textbook derivation of Poisson's adiabatic law. It appears essentially verbatim in Riemann's published 1860 Luftwellen paper, so this page is simply its draft.

checkable.sympy: p,v,R=symbols('p v R',positive=True); T=p*v/R; simplify(diff(T,v)*v/T)==1 and simplify(diff(T,p)*p/T)==1
checkable.asserts: dlogT/dlogv = dlogT/dlogp = 1 under the ideal gas law

checkable.sympy: p,v,R,c,cp=symbols('p v R c cp',positive=True); T=p*v/R; simplify(c*diff(T,v) - T*c/v)==0 and simplify(cp*diff(T,p) - T*cp/p)==0
checkable.asserts: c dT/dv dv + c' dT/dp dp equals T(c dlog v + c' dlog p); here cp stands for Riemann's c'

checkable.sympy: v,C,k=symbols('v C k',positive=True); p=C*v**(-k); simplify(diff(log(p),v) + k*diff(log(v),v))==0
checkable.asserts: p = C v^(-k) satisfies dlog p = -k dlog v, i.e. the adiabatic law log p = -k log v + const

transcription_corrections: The final fragment 'hält[?] sich[?] diese' more likely reads 'bestätigt sich diese' (the experiments of Regnault, Joule and W. Thomson confirm the assumption); this is uncertain from the image.
The struck-out first word of the last paragraph is uncertain; it could be 'Durch' or 'Nach'. The sentence evidently continues 'neueren Versuchen von Regnault, Joule und W. Thomson'.
Margin note at top right is illegible and may not be 'Logarithmen'; it is probably an insertion or correction (possibly 'Boyle'schen', echoing the insertion on the previous page).

In 'so wird [-man-] dieselbe', the word is probably 'derselben' or 'dieser', referring to the unit weight of gas, with 'aufgenommen' completing the clause. The margin '[Gewichtseinheit' supports reading it as a reference to the unit weight.
